ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: US Expansion to 1877 Description: Students will acquaint themselves with secondary scholarship and primary sources on the early history of U.S. expansion. The decades between the birth of the nation and end of Reconstruction saw the formal additions of continental territory through diplomatic, military, and extralegal means and attempts to invade Central America and the Caribbean to extend slavery. Continental expansion was coupled with the annexation of islands in the Pacific and Caribbean and the formation of treaties with Asian countries to gain access to products, markets, and human labor. Students will study these historical developments with an emphasis on the ways in which race, gender, and sexuality shaped and were shaped by the trajectories of U.S. expansion.
